Chapter 8. The Call to Perseverance in the Face of Suffering.
There are times when the cost of following your calling feels almost too heavy to bear. You know those moments—when loss, rejection, or being misunderstood aren't just distant possibilities, but real challenges you’re facing right now. The urge to just walk away, to slip back into what’s familiar or even grow a little cynical, can feel pretty overwhelming.
Imagine someone who’s poured their heart into helping others, only to be met with ingratitude, or even betrayal. That kind of disappointment cuts deep, doesn’t it? Friends might tell them, “Stop caring so much. Just look out for yourself.” But there’s something inside that just won’t let go. It’s like a memory of a deeper calling, or a sense of purpose, that keeps pushing them forward.
Most of us hope that doing the right thing will lead to good things—reward, recognition, maybe even a little peace. Suffering? That’s not what we signed up for. But if you look at the stories of people who’ve walked this path before us, you’ll notice something different. Time and again, the journey of faith leads straight through hardship.
Yet, here’s where it gets interesting. In the middle of suffering, something unexpected starts to happen. You find yourself growing stronger. Your compassion for others gets deeper. The things that once seemed so important just... fade away. And what’s left is this quiet, unshakeable hope.
Now, perseverance isn’t about just gritting your teeth and pretending the pain doesn’t matter. It’s about holding tight to what’s true, even when everything else seems to fall apart. It means trusting that this journey you’re on is worth it, even when you can’t see where it’s leading.
Over time, people who keep going—who refuse to give in—become a source of encouragement for everyone around them. Their stories remind us that suffering isn’t the end of the story. Even in the hardest places, there’s meaning to be found. And in the end, the cost of discipleship is more than matched by the joy and depth that comes from staying the course.
